ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Epoch-wise controller for joint training configuration
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-101 on MS-COCO with a small controller network that, after every epoch, chooses augmentation strength, optimizer momentum, a learning rate multiplier and the mix between binary cross-entropy and asymmetric loss. Feed the controller the validation average precision of the rarest fifth of labels, the loss trend and the gradient norm. Evaluate mean average precision, tail-label average precision, epochs needed to reach 95 percent of the final score and the spread of validation score across epochs.
CONTROLS: Compare with the best static configuration from random search with the same number of full trials, with controllers that adapt a single component, and with a controller whose decisions are replayed in permuted epoch order. Use three seeds each and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Tail-label average precision should rise by about two points over the tuned static run and training should settle in fewer epochs. The approach loses its edge if the permuted-order controller performs as well, since then timing carries no information.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Plateau and co-occurrence drift rules for phase-wise reconfiguration
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-50 on PASCAL VOC and NUS-WIDE with a rule-based scheduler that watches the validation curve and the label co-occurrence matrix computed on recent mini-batches. When the validation score plateaus, the scheduler reduces augmentation, lowers the learning rate by a fixed factor and raises the weight of the loss term for rare labels. When co-occurrence statistics drift, it switches the optimizer from momentum to an adaptive variant. Report mean average precision, rare-label average precision and epochs to reach ninety-five percent of the final score.
CONTROLS: Compare with the best static configuration from random search on equal trial counts, with the same rules applied to one component at a time, and with rules triggered at fixed epochs. Use three seeds each and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 180
PREDICTION: Rare-label average precision should improve by about one point and convergence should come a few epochs earlier than with the static run. Rules that fire at fixed epochs may do as well, which would show that state signals add little.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Small-population training of the joint configuration
PROPOSAL: Train eight copies of a ResNet-101 on MS-COCO in parallel, each with its own augmentation strength, optimizer, learning rate schedule and loss mix. Every few epochs, replace the worst copies by perturbed copies of the best ones, so the configuration changes over time and the best trajectory emerges on its own. Evaluate mean average precision, tail-label average precision, epochs to reach ninety-five percent of the final score and score variance across restarts. Count the total training cost of the population and compare it with the cost of a full offline search.
CONTROLS: Compare with the best static configuration found by random search on the same total compute, with a population that never changes its settings, and with a population that changes only the learning rate. Run three seeds each and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: The population should reach higher tail-label average precision than the best static run at similar total compute. The advantage is doubtful if the frozen population matches the adaptive one.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Online Bayesian proposals driven by gradient statistics
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-101 on MS-COCO while a Gaussian process proposes, at the end of every epoch, the next augmentation strength, learning rate multiplier, optimizer momentum and loss mix. The process takes as inputs the per-label gradient norms, the validation average precision of rare labels and the epoch index. Evaluate mean average precision, tail-label average precision, epochs to reach ninety-five percent of the final score and the number of unstable epochs where validation score drops sharply. Report all four quantities for ten restarts.
CONTROLS: Compare with the best static configuration from random search at equal trial counts, with an epoch-wise controller that sees only the epoch index, and with a proposer that ignores gradient statistics. Run three seeds each and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: Unstable epochs should become rarer and tail-label average precision should rise by one to two points. State inputs give nothing extra if the epoch-index-only controller matches the full one.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hypergradient adaptation of rates, loss weights and augmentation probability
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-50 on PASCAL VOC and MS-COCO while updating the learning rate, the weights of the positive and negative loss terms and the probability of strong augmentation by gradient descent on the validation loss, using a differentiable relaxation of the augmentation choice. Evaluate mean average precision, tail-label average precision, epochs to reach ninety-five percent of the final score and the extra time per epoch compared with a static run.
CONTROLS: Compare with the best static configuration from random search at equal trial counts, with hypergradient updates on one component only, and with updates that use training loss instead of validation loss. Run three seeds each and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: Tail-label average precision should rise by about one point with a modest time overhead per epoch. Overfitting of the validation split may erase the gain, which a held-out test split will reveal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Bandit controller over component presets at phase boundaries
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-101 on MS-COCO and NUS-WIDE in eight phases of equal length. At each boundary a contextual bandit picks one preset from a small menu that sets augmentation strength, optimizer, learning rate and loss mix, and the bandit observes the change in validation tail-label average precision as its reward. Evaluate mean average precision, tail-label average precision, epochs to reach ninety-five percent of the final score and the entropy of the bandit's choices across phases.
CONTROLS: Compare with the best static configuration from random search at equal trial counts, with a bandit that picks presets at random, and with a staged schedule fixed by hand. Run three seeds each and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 250
PREDICTION: The bandit should settle on aggressive augmentation early and on gentler settings for rare labels later. Its reward signal is too noisy if its choices match those of the random picker.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Recurrent controller trained on proxy runs and applied to full training
PROPOSAL: Train a recurrent controller with policy gradients on many short runs of a small ResNet over a reduced MS-COCO subset, rewarding gains in tail-label average precision. Then apply the frozen controller to full training of a ResNet-101 on MS-COCO and of a vision transformer on NUS-WIDE, letting it set augmentation strength, optimizer, learning rate and loss mix every epoch. Evaluate mean average precision, tail-label average precision, epochs to reach ninety-five percent of the final score and score variance across restarts.
CONTROLS: Compare with the best static configuration from random search at equal trial counts, with a controller trained on shuffled state sequences, and with a controller trained on the full task directly. Run three seeds each and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: The transferred controller should match the directly trained one on tail-label average precision at a fraction of the search cost. The proxy runs may be too unlike full training to transfer, in which case the controller falls behind the static run.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Coupling the loss shape to augmentation strength
PROPOSAL: Couple the focusing parameter of an asymmetric loss to the augmentation strength so that both ease together when rare labels stall and tighten together when frequent labels dominate the gradient. Train a ResNet-50 on PASCAL VOC and MS-COCO with this coupled schedule driven by validation average precision of rare labels. Evaluate mean average precision, tail-label average precision, epochs to reach ninety-five percent of the final score and training stability measured as the variance of validation score across epochs.
CONTROLS: Compare with the best static configuration from random search at equal trial counts, with adaptive loss shape and fixed augmentation, and with adaptive augmentation and fixed loss shape. Run three seeds each and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: The coupled schedule should beat both single-component variants on tail-label average precision. If the two single-component variants add up to the same gain, the interaction claim lacks support.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Curriculum over label difficulty with phase-aware optimizer changes
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-101 on MS-COCO and NUS-WIDE with a curriculum that ranks labels by recent validation average precision and upweights the hardest quarter during each phase. In step with the curriculum, the controller lowers augmentation strength for those labels, shortens the learning rate cycle and moves from a momentum optimizer to an adaptive one after the first third of training. Evaluate mean average precision, tail-label average precision, epochs to reach ninety-five percent of the final score and score variance across restarts.
CONTROLS: Compare with the best static configuration from random search at equal trial counts, with the curriculum alone, and with the optimizer switch alone. Run three seeds each and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: Tail-label average precision should rise by about two points and training should settle sooner. The joint schedule adds little if the curriculum alone reaches the same score.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cross-dataset transfer of a meta-learned configuration policy
PROPOSAL: Meta-train a configuration policy on three multi-label datasets, PASCAL VOC, NUS-WIDE and a subset of Open Images, rewarding tail-label average precision gains, then apply it unchanged to MS-COCO with a ResNet-101. The policy sets augmentation strength, optimizer, learning rate multiplier and loss mix every epoch. Evaluate mean average precision, tail-label average precision, epochs to reach ninety-five percent of the final score and the compute spent on meta-training compared with a full offline search on MS-COCO.
CONTROLS: Compare with the best static configuration from random search on MS-COCO at equal trial counts, with a policy meta-trained on MS-COCO itself, and with a policy fed permuted state features. Run three seeds each and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: The transferred policy should come within about a point of the in-domain policy on tail-label average precision. Transfer breaks down if the permuted-feature policy gains as much as the transferred one.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Epoch-wise joint controller compared with tuned static training
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-101 on MS-COCO with a small controller that, after every epoch, selects augmentation strength, optimizer momentum, a learning rate multiplier and the mix of binary cross-entropy and asymmetric loss. Feed it the validation average precision of the rarest fifth of labels, the loss trend and the gradient norm. Evaluate mean average precision, tail-label average precision, epochs to reach 95 percent of the final score, and the spread of validation score across epochs.
CONTROLS: Compare against the best static configuration found by random search with the same number of full training trials at the same input resolution. Compare against controllers that adapt a single component, same state features. Compare against a controller whose decisions are replayed in permuted epoch order, same set of values. Repeat each run with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 520
PREDICTION: Tail-label average precision should rise by about two points over the tuned static run, and training should settle in fewer epochs. The idea is refuted if the permuted-order controller reaches the same score as the intact one.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Epoch-wise joint controller compared with default recipes
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-101 on MS-COCO using a compact controller that, once per epoch, picks augmentation strength, optimizer momentum, a learning rate multiplier and the blend of binary cross-entropy and asymmetric loss. Its inputs are the rarest fifth of labels' validation average precision, the loss trend and the gradient norm. Report mean average precision, average precision on the tail labels, the epoch at which 95 percent of the final score is reached, and the validation score spread over epochs.
CONTROLS: Compare against the default static configuration of a common recipe, with random flips only, same number of epochs. Compare against static runs with a deeper backbone, same input resolution. Compare against a controller trained on another dataset, same set of values. Repeat each run with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 520
PREDICTION: Tail-label average precision should rise by about two points over the default recipe, and training should settle in fewer epochs. The idea is refuted if the cross-dataset controller reaches the same score as the intact one.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Update interval and state features of a joint training controller
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-50 on PASCAL VOC and NUS-WIDE with a controller that rewrites augmentation strength, optimizer momentum, learning rate and loss weights at set intervals during training. It reads the validation average precision of rare labels, the label co-occurrence drift between recent mini-batches and the gradient norm. Evaluate mean average precision, rare-label average precision, convergence epoch and score variance across restarts.
CONTROLS: Vary the update interval across every epoch, every few epochs and every phase, same input resolution. Compare the full state against a version that drops the co-occurrence drift, same interval. Compare the controller against the same one with the loss weights held fixed. Repeat each configuration with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 1400
PREDICTION: Shorter intervals and the drift feature should each add a fraction of a point on rare-label average precision. The adaptive design is called into question if frozen loss weights give the same score as the full controller.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Backbone width and input resolution around a joint training controller
PROPOSAL: Fit a ResNet-50 of varying width to NUS-WIDE and PASCAL VOC under a controller that rewrites augmentation strength, optimizer momentum, learning rate and loss weights every few epochs. The controller reads rare-label validation average precision, co-occurrence drift between recent mini-batches and gradient norms. Measure mean average precision, rare-label average precision, convergence epoch and the variance of scores over restarts.
CONTROLS: Vary the backbone width across narrow, standard and wide, same state features. Compare the standard input resolution against a larger one, same interval. Compare the controller against the same one with the data loader workers held fixed. Repeat each configuration with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 1400
PREDICTION: Wider backbones and larger images should each add a fraction of a point on rare-label average precision. The adaptive design is called into question if worker counts give the same score as the full controller.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Rare-label behaviour of adaptive configuration on the full label set
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-50 on MS-COCO with all 80 labels, whose frequencies span two orders of magnitude, using a controller that adjusts augmentation strength, learning rate multiplier and loss weights every epoch from the validation average precision of the 20 rarest labels. Evaluate mean average precision, average precision on the rare labels, the epoch at which 95 percent of the final score is reached, and the score variance across restarts.
CONTROLS: Compare against the best static configuration on the full label set, same number of epochs. Compare against a controller with loss weights held fixed, same label set. Compare per-label average precision for the rarest and the most frequent labels, same restarts. Repeat each run with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 260
PREDICTION: Rare-label average precision should rise by a point or two while frequent labels stay put. The controller is refuted if the static run matches its rare-label score on the full label set.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive configuration on a frequent-label subset with short training
PROPOSAL: Fit a ResNet-50 on the 20 most frequent MS-COCO labels, whose counts differ by a factor of three at most, with a controller tuning augmentation strength, learning rate multiplier and loss weights after each epoch from validation scores of the same labels. Measure mean average precision, average precision of the weakest labels, the epoch where 95 percent of the final score appears and the variance of scores over restarts.
CONTROLS: Compare against the best static configuration on the frequent subset, same number of epochs. Compare against a controller with loss weights held fixed, same label subset. Compare per-label average precision for the weakest and the strongest labels, same restarts. Repeat each run with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 260
PREDICTION: Average precision on the weakest labels should rise by a point or two while the strongest stay put. The controller is refuted if the static run matches its weakest-label score on the frequent subset.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Validation-driven joint controller judged on held-out label scores
PROPOSAL: Train a ViT-Base on NUS-WIDE with a controller that picks augmentation strength, optimizer, learning rate multiplier and loss mix at the start of each epoch, reading the validation average precision of tail labels and the loss trend. Evaluate on a held-out test split, and log everything per epoch.
CONTROLS: Compare test mean average precision against the best static configuration, same number of epochs. Compare test average precision of the tail labels against the same run. Compare the epoch at which 95 percent of the final test score is reached against the same run. Repeat each run with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Test score on tail labels should rise by about two points and convergence should come sooner. The controller is refuted if test scores stay within seed noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training dynamics under a joint controller
PROPOSAL: Train a ViT-Base on NUS-WIDE with a controller that picks augmentation strength, optimizer, learning rate multiplier and loss mix at the start of each epoch, reading the training loss slope and the gradient norm. Log the loss, the gradient norm and the update size every step, and compare final values.
CONTROLS: Compare final training loss against the best static configuration, same number of epochs. Compare the peak gradient norm of the tail labels against the same run. Compare the epoch at which 95 percent of the final training loss is reached against the same run. Repeat each run with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Training loss should fall faster and the peak gradient norm should shrink by a few percent. The controller is refuted if these curves stay within seed noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Joint adaptive configuration with a time-order check on a large benchmark
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-101 on MS-COCO and a vision transformer on Open Images with a controller that reconfigures augmentation, optimizer, learning rate and loss every epoch, using validation average precision of rare labels, the loss trend and gradient norms as inputs. Evaluate mean average precision, tail-label average precision, convergence epoch and score variance across restarts, and measure the controller's own overhead per epoch.
CONTROLS: Compare against the best static configuration from random search at the same number of full trials. Compare against a controller whose decisions are permuted in time, same set of values. Compare against controllers adapting a single component, same inputs. Repeat each run with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: Tail-label average precision should rise by two points and convergence should come sooner. The idea is called into question if the permuted controller reaches the same score, meaning timing is irrelevant.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Two initializations of a joint adaptive controller on a large benchmark
PROPOSAL: Fit a ResNet-101 to MS-COCO and a vision transformer to Open Images under a controller that retunes augmentation, optimizer, learning rate and loss at each epoch, reading rare-label validation scores, loss trends and gradient norms. Score mean average precision, rare-label average precision, the epoch of convergence, the variance across restarts and the time the controller adds per epoch.
CONTROLS: Compare against the best static configuration from random search at the same number of full trials. Compare against a controller that starts from different initial weights, same set of values. Compare against controllers adapting a single component, same inputs. Repeat each run with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: Rare-label scores should improve by two points and training should converge sooner. Doubt arises if the differently initialized controller lands on the same score, meaning initial weights are irrelevant.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Epoch-wise controller that sets all four training components from the learning state
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-101 on MS-COCO and PASCAL VOC with a controller network that, each epoch, sets augmentation strength, optimizer momentum, learning rate multiplier and loss mix from validation tail-label average precision, loss trend and gradient norm. Evaluate mean average precision, tail-label average precision, epochs to reach 95 percent of the final score and the validation spread across epochs.
CONTROLS: Compare against the best static configuration from random search with equal trial counts and against controllers adapting one component at a time. Include a controller replayed in permuted epoch order. Repeat each run with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 450
PREDICTION: Tail-label average precision should rise by about two points over the tuned static run with smoother validation curves. The adaptive design adds little if the permuted-order controller scores the same.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Label-graph head for dependencies among labels in a static training recipe
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-101 on MS-COCO and PASCAL VOC with a graph convolution head built on label co-occurrence statistics, under a fixed augmentation, optimizer, learning rate schedule and loss. Evaluate mean average precision, tail-label average precision, epochs to reach 95 percent of the final score and the validation spread across epochs, comparing the head against a linear classifier on the same backbone.
CONTROLS: Compare against the linear head with the same tuned static configuration and against a head that uses a co-occurrence matrix with entries permuted. Include a transformer-based label head. Repeat each run with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 450
PREDICTION: Tail-label average precision should rise by about one point from modelling label dependencies. The head adds little if the permuted-matrix version scores the same.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Phase-triggered reconfiguration based on label co-occurrence drift
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-50 on PASCAL VOC with a rule-based scheduler that monitors the co-occurrence matrix of recent mini-batches and the validation curve. When drift or a plateau appears, the scheduler changes augmentation strength, learning rate, optimizer and the weight on rare-label loss terms. Evaluate mean average precision, rare-label average precision and epochs to reach 95 percent of the final score.
CONTROLS: Compare against the best static configuration from random search at equal trial counts, against rules triggered at fixed epochs and against rules acting on one component. Repeat each run with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 140
PREDICTION: Rare-label average precision should rise by about a point and convergence should come a few epochs sooner. Rules that fire on state add little if fixed-epoch rules match them.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Threshold calibration after static training
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-50 on PASCAL VOC under a tuned static recipe, then calibrate a decision threshold for each label on the validation split by maximizing its F-score, and re-calibrate on a second held-out split. Evaluate mean average precision, rare-label F-score and the stability of the thresholds across the two splits, to check how much final scoring gains from calibration.
CONTROLS: Compare against a single global threshold, against per-label thresholds fitted on the training split and against rank-based cutoffs. Repeat each run with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 140
PREDICTION: Rare-label F-score should rise by about a point and thresholds should stay stable across splits. Calibration adds little if global thresholds score the same.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Bandit selection of component presets at phase boundaries
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-101 on MS-COCO for 120 epochs in 8 phases, with a contextual bandit that picks at each boundary one of 6 presets for augmentation strength, optimizer, learning rate and loss mix, rewarded by the change in validation tail-label average precision. Evaluate mean average precision, tail-label average precision, epochs to reach 95 percent of the final score and the entropy of the bandit's choices.
CONTROLS: Compare against the best static configuration from random search at equal trial counts, against a bandit that picks presets at random and against a hand-written staged schedule. Repeat each run with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 1100
PREDICTION: The bandit should favour strong augmentation early and gentler settings for rare labels later, lifting tail-label average precision by a point or two. Its reward is too noisy if its choices match the random picker.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Longer static training and larger batches on MS-COCO
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-101 on MS-COCO for 40, 80 and 160 epochs under a tuned static recipe, scaling batch size and learning rate together, to see how final mean average precision and tail-label average precision depend on training length. Evaluate epochs to reach 95 percent of the best final score and the validation spread across epochs for each length.
CONTROLS: Compare each length against the shortest run with the same tuned recipe, against a cosine schedule and against a step schedule. Include a run with larger batches only. Repeat each run with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 1100
PREDICTION: Final scores should rise with training length with diminishing returns, and tail labels should gain the most. Longer training adds little if the gain between the two longest runs stays within seed noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transferred configuration policy meta-trained on related datasets
PROPOSAL: Meta-train a configuration policy on PASCAL VOC and NUS-WIDE with a reward based on tail-label average precision, then apply it unchanged to MS-COCO with a ResNet-101, setting augmentation strength, optimizer, learning rate multiplier and loss mix every epoch. Evaluate mean average precision, tail-label average precision, epochs to reach 95 percent of the final score and the cost of meta-training.
CONTROLS: Compare against the best static configuration from random search on MS-COCO, against a policy meta-trained on MS-COCO itself and against a policy fed permuted state features. Repeat each run with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 360
PREDICTION: The transferred policy should land within a point of the in-domain policy on tail-label average precision. Transfer breaks down if the permuted-feature policy scores the same.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Distilling a larger teacher into a ResNet-101 for rare labels
PROPOSAL: Distill a vision transformer teacher into a ResNet-101 on MS-COCO using soft labels with temperature scaling, under a tuned static recipe for augmentation, optimizer, learning rate schedule and loss. Evaluate mean average precision, tail-label average precision, epochs to reach 95 percent of the final score and the cost of teacher inference.
CONTROLS: Compare against the same student trained without the teacher, against a student distilled from a teacher of its own architecture and against distillation with permuted soft labels. Repeat each run with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 360
PREDICTION: Tail-label average precision should rise by about two points with the teacher. Distillation adds little if the permuted-label version scores the same.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hypergradient adaptation of rates, loss weights and augmentation probability
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-50 on PASCAL VOC and MS-COCO, updating the learning rate, the weights of the positive and negative loss terms and the probability of strong augmentation by gradient steps on a validation loss, with a differentiable relaxation of the augmentation choice. Evaluate mean average precision, tail-label average precision, epochs to reach 95 percent of the final score and the time per epoch against a static run.
CONTROLS: Compare against the best static configuration from random search at equal trial counts, against hypergradient updates on one component only and against updates driven by training loss. Repeat each run with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 2200
PREDICTION: Tail-label average precision should rise by about a point at modest overhead per epoch. Overfitting of the validation split may erase the gain, which a held-out test split will reveal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Class-balanced resampling fixed before training
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-50 on PASCAL VOC and MS-COCO after resampling the training set once so that every label appears with a similar frequency, using repeat factors computed from label counts, and keep augmentation, optimizer, learning rate schedule and loss static. Evaluate mean average precision, tail-label average precision, epochs to reach 95 percent of the final score and the time per epoch against an unresampled run.
CONTROLS: Compare against the unresampled tuned static configuration, against resampling with repeat factors permuted across labels and against loss re-weighting by label counts. Repeat each run with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 2200
PREDICTION: Tail-label average precision should rise by about a point at similar time per epoch. Resampling adds little if the permuted-factor version scores the same.
